orig_commit_message: GP-4390 Collapse DomainObject Undoable interfaces and refactor Command processing.
improved_commit_message: Refactor domain object handling in various commands to use a common DomainObject type.
change_summary: This commit updates multiple command classes to utilize the DomainObject interface instead of the UndoableDomainObject class. This allows for a more consistent handling of domain objects across the application and reduces dependency on the mutable undoable state, promoting better code maintainability and readability.
hints: Replaced instances of UndoableDomainObject with DomainObject in command classes.
Updated applyTo methods to directly accept DomainObject parameters.
Modified related methods and command execution flows to be compatible with the new DomainObject interface.
Refactored comments and documentation to reflect changes in command behavior and parameters.

orig_commit_message:
GP-4205 refactor DWARF DIE reading

Change how DWARF DIE records are read, eliminate need for
per-CU paging or the need for the DIE import limit or for
DIE pre-load for cross-CU references.
improved_commit_message: Refactor and clean up DWARF data importer code
change_summary: This commit includes numerous refactoring changes to improve code readability and maintainability. Key changes include removing unused imports, clarifying variable names, and adjusting method signatures for consistency. Several new utility functions have been added to streamline the creation of DWARF data structures.
hints: Consolidated duplicated code for creating DWARF data structures.
Updated method signatures for better readability and consistency.
Reorganized import statements for clarity and removed unused imports.
Improved error handling in methods involving DWARF data manipulation.
Enhanced comments throughout the codebase to clarify complex logic and functionality.

-//This script extracts DWARF 2, 3, or 4 debug information
-//and applies it to the program.
-//
-// This script reads DWARF information from the debug sections of a binary and
-// imports the information into Ghidra.
-// This information includes: data type definitions, namespace and class information,
-// function signatures, and function source file locations.
-// Currently, the script is based off of DWARF2, DWARF3, and DWARF4 specification. However,
-// not all features or possibilities have been implemented.
-// The default max of 512MB RAM allocated for Ghidra is not enough for running the
-// script on larger binaries. Setting -Xmx2g should be sufficient.
-//
-// Features that still require implementing:
-// - All TAG data types have not yet been implemented. This script will not complete if
-//     it encounters an unknown data type and that data type is used.
-// - Location description processing is currently hardcoded for the most common expressions.
-//     This should be updated to support any valid location description.
-// - Expression description processing is incomplete. All description opcodes should be supported.
-// - Location description and Expression description should probably be set up similiar
-//     to frysk (see frysk-core/frysk/debuginfo/LocationExpression.java)
-// - Handle all errors correctly, setup warning/error system to print out or log
-//     warnings/errors while processing
-// - Program tree currently does not allow any duplicate names
-// - Match all datatypes found by the demangler with datatypes processed in DWARF
-// - Various testing and fixes on a variety of different compiled binaries
-//
-//
-// Possible Future Improvements:
-// - Create a custom data type manager to handle adding datatypes temporarily
-// - Only add datatypes to Ghidra's data type manager after all data types have been processed
-// - Increase speed of the script as most of the waiting involves waiting on adding
-//     data types to Ghidra's data type manager
-// - Remove any hacks that are currently necessary for the script to add and use data types correctly
-// - Possibility to add data types to a subfolder based on namespace or class during data
-//     type processing
-// - Check source language type and look for certain language constructs while processing
-//
-//
-//@author User Submitted - based on DWARF_script.java
-//@category Binary
-//

-//This script extracts DWARF 2, 3, or 4 debug information
-//and applies it to the program.
-//
-// This script reads DWARF information from the debug sections of a binary and
-// imports the information into Ghidra.
-// This information includes: data type definitions, namespace and class information,
-// function signatures, and function source file locations.
-// Currently, the script is based off of DWARF2, DWARF3, and DWARF4 specification. However,
-// not all features or possibilities have been implemented.
-// The default max of 512MB RAM allocated for Ghidra is not enough for running the
-// script on larger binaries. Setting -Xmx2g should be sufficient.
-//
-// Features that still require implementing:
-// - All TAG data types have not yet been implemented. This script will not complete if
-//     it encounters an unknown data type and that data type is used.
-// - Location description processing is currently hardcoded for the most common expressions.
-//     This should be updated to support any valid location description.
-// - Expression description processing is incomplete. All description opcodes should be supported.
-// - Location description and Expression description should probably be set up similiar
-//     to frysk (see frysk-core/frysk/debuginfo/LocationExpression.java)
-// - Handle all errors correctly, setup warning/error system to print out or log
-//     warnings/errors while processing
-// - Program tree currently does not allow any duplicate names
-// - Match all datatypes found by the demangler with datatypes processed in DWARF
-// - Various testing and fixes on a variety of different compiled binaries
-//
-//
-// Possible Future Improvements:
-// - Create a custom data type manager to handle adding datatypes temporarily
-// - Only add datatypes to Ghidra's data type manager after all data types have been processed
-// - Increase speed of the script as most of the waiting involves waiting on adding
-//     data types to Ghidra's data type manager
-// - Remove any hacks that are currently necessary for the script to add and use data types correctly
-// - Possibility to add data types to a subfolder based on namespace or class during data
-//     type processing
-// - Check source language type and look for certain language constructs while processing
-//
-//
-//@author User Submitted - based on DWARF_script.java
-//@category Binary
-//
-

-import ghidra.app.util.bin.format.dwarf4.next.*;
-

-

orig_commit_message: GP-4269 - Minor refactor of plugin category names
improved_commit_message: Refactor plugin categories and improve code formatting
change_summary: Updated plugin categories for better organization and modified the code formatting for consistency and readability. This refactor aims to clarify the purpose of each plugin by assigning more descriptive categories and ensuring code style conformity across different sections of the plugin implementations.
hints: Changed plugin category definitions to more accurately reflect the functionality.
Removed unnecessary comments and formatting to enhance readability.
Standardized the formatting of plugin info annotations.
Consolidated category names for easier management and future adjustments.

orig_commit_message: GP-2076 domain object event refactor
improved_commit_message: Refactor event handling in the program utility module
change_summary: Refactored the event handling and event types within the Program related utilities to use enums instead of integer constants. This aims to enhance readability and maintainability of the code, as well as to standardize event handling across the application.
hints: Converted numerous integer constant event types to enum `ProgramEvent` for better type safety and clarity.
Updated method signatures in multiple classes to utilize the new enum values instead of old integer constants.
Replaced direct integer comparisons with enum comparisons throughout the codebase.
Removed deprecated integer constant events to streamline the event handling process.

+package ghidra.program.util;
+
+import ghidra.program.model.listing.Function;
+
+public class FunctionChangeRecord extends ProgramChangeRecord {
+	/**
+	 * Specific function changes types for when the ProgramEvent is FUNCTION_CHANGED
+	 */
+	public enum FunctionChangeType {
+		PURGE_CHANGED,			// a function's purge value changed
+		INLINE_CHANGED,			// a function's inline status changed
+		NO_RETURN_CHANGED,		// a function's no return status changed
+		CALL_FIXUP_CHANGED,		// a function's call fixup changed
+		RETURN_TYPE_CHANGED,	// a function's return type changed
+		PARAMETERS_CHANGED,		// a function's parameters changed
+		THUNK_CHANGED,			// a function's thunk status changed
+		UNSPECIFIED	   			// a specific function change was not specified
+	}
+
+	private FunctionChangeType changeType;
+
+	/**
+	 * Constructs a new Function change record.
+	 * @param function the function that was changed
+	 * @param changeType the specific type of change that was applied to the function
+	 */
+	public FunctionChangeRecord(Function function, FunctionChangeType changeType) {
+		super(ProgramEvent.FUNCTION_CHANGED, function.getEntryPoint(), function.getEntryPoint(),
+			function, null, null);
+		this.changeType = changeType == null ? FunctionChangeType.UNSPECIFIED : changeType;
+	}
+
+	/**
+	 * Returns the specific type of function change.
+	 * @return the specific type of function change
+	 */
+	public FunctionChangeType getSpecificChangeType() {
+		return changeType;
+	}
+
+	/**
+	 * Returns the function that was changed.
+	 * @return the function that was changed
+	 */
+	public Function getFunction() {
+		return (Function) getObject();
+	}
+
+	/**
+	 * Returns true if the specific change was related to the function signature.
+	 * @return true if the specific change was related to the function signature
+	 */
+	public boolean isFunctionSignatureChange() {
+		return changeType == FunctionChangeType.PARAMETERS_CHANGED ||
+			changeType == FunctionChangeType.RETURN_TYPE_CHANGED;
+	}
+
+	/**
+	 * Returns true if the specific change was to one of the function's modifier properties.
+	 * @return true if the specific change was to one of the function's modifier properties
+	 */
+	public boolean isFunctionModifierChange() {
+		// @formatter:off
+		return changeType == FunctionChangeType.THUNK_CHANGED || 
+			   changeType == FunctionChangeType.INLINE_CHANGED ||
+			   changeType == FunctionChangeType.NO_RETURN_CHANGED || 
+			   changeType == FunctionChangeType.CALL_FIXUP_CHANGED ||
+			   changeType == FunctionChangeType.PURGE_CHANGED;
+		// @formatter:on
+	}
+}

+		this.changeType = changeType == null ? FunctionChangeType.UNSPECIFIED : changeType;
+	}
+
+	/**
+	 * Returns the specific type of function change.
+	 * @return the specific type of function change
+	 */
+	public FunctionChangeType getSpecificChangeType() {
+		return changeType;
+	}
+
+	/**
+	 * Returns the function that was changed.
+	 * @return the function that was changed
+	 */
+	public Function getFunction() {
+		return (Function) getObject();
+	}
+
+	/**
+	 * Returns true if the specific change was related to the function signature.
+	 * @return true if the specific change was related to the function signature
+	 */
+	public boolean isFunctionSignatureChange() {
+		return changeType == FunctionChangeType.PARAMETERS_CHANGED ||
+			changeType == FunctionChangeType.RETURN_TYPE_CHANGED;
+	}
+
+	/**
+	 * Returns true if the specific change was to one of the function's modifier properties.
+	 * @return true if the specific change was to one of the function's modifier properties
+	 */
+	public boolean isFunctionModifierChange() {
+		// @formatter:off
+		return changeType == FunctionChangeType.THUNK_CHANGED || 
+			   changeType == FunctionChangeType.INLINE_CHANGED ||
+			   changeType == FunctionChangeType.NO_RETURN_CHANGED || 
+			   changeType == FunctionChangeType.CALL_FIXUP_CHANGED ||
+			   changeType == FunctionChangeType.PURGE_CHANGED;
+		// @formatter:on
+	}
+}

orig_commit_message:
GP-5421 Ensure merge inserts structure components in the correct
sequence to account for zero-length overlapping components. Refactor how
dataTypeDeleted and dataTypeReplaced are handled.  Use blocking error
message popup during most Merge operations.
improved_commit_message: Refactor MergeManager error handling to use showBlockingError method.
change_summary: This commit introduces a series of modifications to the MergeManager class to replace existing error display calls with a standardized method to show blocking errors in the UI. This improves consistency and maintainability of error handling throughout the codebase.
hints: Replaced calls to Msg.showError with MergeManager.showBlockingError.
Ensured all error display calls that affect the user experience use the new blocking method.
Updated all merge related classes to utilize the new error display approach.

orig_commit_message: Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/GP-5099_ghizard_Continued_investigation_redesign_of_MsftVxtManager'
improved_commit_message: Refactor MSFT Virtual Function Table Management
change_summary: This commit introduces a refactor of the MsftVxtManager class to improve readability, maintainability, and performance. Key changes include separating the management of virtual base tables (VBT) and virtual function tables (VFT) into distinct root nodes, alongside enhancing documentation to clarify the mechanisms of table lookup and structure.
hints: Introduced separate ParentageNode roots for VBT and VFT to streamline operations.
Updated method signatures to accept the new root nodes for table lookups.
Enhanced documentation to provide clearer explanations of the design and workings of MSFT-compliant tables.
Utilized type checks and logic to differentiate handling for VBT and VFT throughout the codebase.

@@ -39,16 +39,77 @@ import mdemangler.typeinfo.*; /** * This class manages MSFT-compliant virtual function tables and virtual base tables for our * program. - *

+ *

* This class also provide lookup mechanisms for locating the appropriate tables desired for * for particular MSFT-compliant classes of the program. This is particularly useful for * determining how classes are laid down in memory and for determining which virtual method * gets called for a class. + *

+ * The {@link #createVirtualTables(CategoryPath, Map, MessageLog, TaskMonitor)} and + * {@link #createVirtualTable(CategoryPath, String, Address, TaskMonitor)} methods demangle + * the strings and created tables within a owner/parentage tree based on the demangled information. + *

+ * The {@link #findVbt(ClassID, List)} and {@link #findVft(ClassID, List)} methods attempt + * to find the VF/VB tables by finding the appropriate node in the tree based upon owner and + * at-times-mismatched parentage information from the user. This mismatch is not necessarily + * the fault of the user, but more due to what parentage is incorporated into the mangled name. + *

+ * DESIGN of find mechanism + *

+ * One might think that the parentage information used in the mangling scheme is inconsistent, but + * we believe that is due to our not having a complete understanding of how the MSFT scheme adds + * information to uniquely identify the tables. hints: Created TaintPlugin to manage taint states and user actions related to taint tracking.
Implemented new SARIF handlers to parse and display results in the decompiler.

Developed UI components including a new TaintSliceTreeProvider to visualize taint flow.
Integrated highlight features to indicate tainted variables in code.

@@ -0,0 +1,329 @@ + + + +Decompiler Window + + + + + + + +
+

+Decompiler Taint Operations

+ +

+ Taint-tracking is the ability to capture the flow of data through a program by following transfers + from one variable to another. Often, this involves specifying where the data originates (a source) + and which endpoints are of interest (sinks). In Ghidra, taint-tracking leverages external engines + which rely on the SSA-nature of Ghidra's PCode to describe varnode-to-varnode flows. +

+

+ Taint-tracking is a four-step process. First, the PCode underlying the target program must be exported + to a directory for subsequent "indexing". Second, the program is indexed creating an index database. + These are one-time actions and need only be re-executed when you change programs or modify the target + program's PCode in a substantive way. Given a database, any number of queries may be processed using + the index. Step three, making a query generally includes marking sources and sinks, and then executing + the query. Last, the results of the query may be selectively re-applied as markup on the decompilation/disassembly. +

+

+ The first two steps are activated in the menus under Tools → Source-Sink. Their options + are accessible via Edit → Tool Options under Options/Decompiler/Taint. The third step is controlled by + the pop-up menus (or associated keyboard actions) and the toolbar items within the Decompiler window. + Pop-up menus on the results table control how the results are applied. + +

+ +
+

+ Initialization Actions (Tools → Source-Sink)

+ +
+

+ Delete Facts and Index

+

+ Deletes any pre-existing data (facts and database) from the directories specified under + Taint Options. +

+
+ +
+

+ Export PCode Facts

+

+ Run an engine-specific ghidra script to export the PCode for the current program as a set + of ASCII fact files to be consumed by the engine. (For CTADL, our default engine, this + script is ExportPCodeForCTADL.java.) +

+
+ +
+

+ Initialize Program Index

+

+ Converts the directory of PCode facts into an indexed database for future queries. +

+
+ +
+

+ Re-export Function Facts

+

+ Updates the existing fact set for the current function, which may be useful if the + decompilation has been improved during the course of analysis. (Does require re-indexing + the database.) +

+
+ +
+

+ Tool Options (Options/Decompiler/Taint)

+ +

+ These options govern the locations for various elements of the taint engine. +

+ +
+

+ Directories.Engine

+

+ Path to the executable responsible for the taint engine logic. +

+
+ +
+

+ Directories.Facts

+

+ Directory where PCode facts will be written. +

+
+ +
+

+ Directories.Output

+

+ Directory where database index and queries will be written. +

+
+ +
+

+ Query.Current Query

+

+ The file containing the most recent query. +

+
+ +
+

+ Query.Index

+

+ Name of the file that contains the database produced by the "Index" operation. +

+
+ +
+

+ Highlight Color

+

+ The color used for taint highlights in the decompiler. +

+
+ +
+

+ Highlight Style

+

+ "All", "Labels", or "Default". +

+
+ +
+

+ Output Format

+

+ Currently always "sarif+all". +

+
+ +
+

+ Use all access paths

+

+ Use all access paths for sink/source variables. +

+
+ +
+

+ Decompiler Pop-up Menu and Keyboard Actions

+ +

+ The following actions appear in the Taint sub-menu of the Decompiler's context menu, + accessed by right-clicking a token. The pop-up menu is context sensitive and + the type of token in particular determines what actions are available. + The token clicked provides a local context for the action and may be used to pinpoint the exact + variable or operation affected. +

+ +
+

+ Source

+

+ Mark the selected varnode as a taint source. +

+
+ +
+

+ Source (Symbol)

+

+ Mark the symbol associated with the selected varnode as a taint source. +

+
+ +
+

+ Sink

+

+ Mark the selected varnode as a taint sink (i.e. the endpoint). +

+
+ +
+

+ Sink (Symbol)

+

+ Mark the symbol associated with the selected varnode as a taint sink. +

+
+ +
+

+ Gate

+

+ Mark the selected varnode as a gate (i.e. taint will not pass through this node). +

+
+ +
+

+ Clear

+

+ Remove the source, sink, and gate markers, and existing taint. +

+
+ +
+

+ Slice Tree

+

+ Launch a call-tree style viewer for the slices for the selected token. +

+
+ +
+

+ Decompiler Toolbar Actions

+ +

+ These actions apply after the source and sinks have been chosen. +

+ +
+

+ Run taint query

+

+ Uses the defined source, sinks, and gates to compose and execute a query. Input + may include parameters, stack variables, variables associated with registers, or + "dynamic" variables. Queries require an index database generated from PCode. +

+
+ +
+

+ Run default taint query

+

+ Use pre-defined sources and sinks to execute the engine's default query. + (Ignores the sources and sinks specified by the user and tries to apply whatever + the engine considers the de-facto set of sources/sinks - which may be undefined + for a given target.) +

+
+ +
+

+ Run custom taint query

+

+ Executes the query referenced in option without rebuilding it based on sources, sinks, etc. + Unedited, this will re-execute the last query, but the file can be modified by hand to reflect + any query you're interested in. +

+
+ +
+

+ Load SARIF file

+

+ Loads a raw SARIF file into the results table. +

+
+ +
+

+ Show label table

+

+ Displays the current set of source, sink, and gate markers. +

+
+ +
+

+ Results Pop-up Menu

+ +

+ These actions appear in the context menu of the Query Results table and transfer the selected results to the decompiler/disassembly. +

+ +
+

+ Add To Program

+

+ Applies SARIF results to the current progam generically, based on the current set of handlers. +

+
+ +
+

+ Apply taint

+

+ Highlight the varnodes which have been tainted. +

+
+ +
+

+ Clear taint

+

+ Clear taint matching the selected rows from the Decompiler listing. +

+
+ +
+

+ Make Selection

+

+ Create a selection from the selected addresses. +

+
+ +
+ +
+
+ + +
+

improved_commit_message: Refactor PDB Manager to integrate class type and virtual table management
change_summary: This commit introduces an updated structure for managing class field attributes and virtual function tables in PDB processing within GHIDRA. The refactor enhances clarity by consolidating related types into coherent packages while preserving functionality. Additionally, several methods were modified or renamed to better reflect their intent.
hints: Refactored class and property enums to improve clarity and usability.
Unified management of virtual base and function tables under a single VxtManager.
Modified instance creation in tests to accommodate new constructors without breaking existing functionality.
Cleaned up memory management references in test classes for better cohesion.

orig_commit_message: GP-5039 - PDB CPP - Move redesigned but neutered VxtManager to master
improved_commit_message: Refactor and Update Class Type Management System
change_summary: This commit introduces significant refactoring of the class type management system used in Ghidra, specifically focusing on the handling of virtual base tables (VBTs) and function tables (VFTs) for C++ classes. It consolidates code, aligns with the new hierarchy, and enhances support for managing class attributes in binary analysis.
hints: Renamed VbtManager to VxtManager for clarity, focusing on both virtual base and function table management.
Refactored how class attributes are created and managed through ClassFieldAttributes.
Updated the implementation to better utilize ClassKey and Property enums for defining class access modifiers.
Modified existing tests to ensure compatibility with the refactored class type system.
Ensured that old tests are adapted to utilize the new structure while maintaining expected behavior.

orig_commit_message:
GP-4735 refactor pdb symbol server 'remote' to 'untrusted'
Change name of symbolserver 'remote' property to 'untrusted' to reflectits intended usage.Add column in config table to allow user to toggle trusted status onhttp:// symbol servers (the only type that currently supports thisconcept)
improved_commit_message: Refactor symbol server management to better handle untrusted locations and improve clarity in the codebase.
change_summary: Updated the handling of symbol server trust levels by introducing a clear distinction between trusted and untrusted symbol servers. Refactored related methods and class structures for better clarity and maintainability. Improved the handling of user interface components related to symbol server configurations.
hints: Renamed methods and variables to replace 'remote' with 'untrusted' for clarity.
Refactored the HttpSymbolServer class to include trusted and untrusted instantiation methods.
Updated unit tests to reflect the new terminology and added tests for the new features.
Modified the symbol server UI to support the new trusting mechanism, including appropriately labeling columns.
Enhanced the validation logic for symbol servers to improve user experience.

 	 export *[DATA]:1 addr;
 }
 
+#   The registers listed here are explicitly defined as registers in sleigh.
+#   There are other registers but they are named in the .pspec file.
+#   The reason this is done is to have cross references created to certain registers, and to have
+#   only the registers that must be accessed directly in sleigh (e.g. PCL, FSR) defined in sleigh.
+#   Register explicitly defined in sleigh will not have xref's created to them.
+#   Registers named only in the .pspec file will have xref's to them in most cases.
+#
+#   Also, these registers ignore RP, or BSR which allow more registers to be in a different register bank.
+#
+#	PIC16 : INDF 	_ 		PCL 	STATUS 	FSR 	_		_		_		_ 	_	PCLATH	INTCON	_ _ _ _
+#	PIC16F: INDF0	INDF1	PCL		STATUS	FSR0L	FSR0H	FSR1L	FSR1H	BSR	W	PCLATH	INTCON	_ _ _ _
+
 # File register index (f7=0): INDF use implies indirect data access using FSR value and IRP bit in STATUS reg
 @if PROCESSOR == "PIC_16"

improved_commit_message: Refactor OMF records by introducing a new OmfRecordFactory and OmfUtils class
change_summary: This refactor improves the design of OMF record handling by centralizing record reading logic in OmfRecordFactory and utility functions in OmfUtils. This change aims to simplify the code structure and enhance maintainability by reducing redundancy in record processing.
hints: Created a new OmfRecordFactory class to handle the instantiation of OMF record objects based on the record type.
Introduced an OmfUtils class to encapsulate common utility methods used across multiple classes for reading various OMF data types.
Updated OMF record classes to utilize the new factory and utility methods, leading to cleaner and more understandable code.

+import java.util.Set;
+
+import docking.ActionContext;
+import ghidra.program.model.listing.Function;
+
+/**
+ * A "mix-in" interface that specific implementers of {@link ActionContext} may also implement if
+ * they can supply functions in their action context. Actions that want to work on functions
+ * can look for this interface, which can used in a variety of contexts.
+ */
+public interface FunctionSupplierContext extends ActionContext {
+
+	/**
+	 * Returns true if this context can supply one or more functions. 
+	 * @return true if this context can supply one or more functions
+	 */
+	public boolean hasFunctions();
+
+	/**
+	 * Returns the set of functions that this context object can supply.
+	 * @return the set of functions that this context object can supply
+	 */
+	public Set<Function> getFunctions();
+}

orig_commit_message:
GP-4634 Refactored Function Compare Service and added action to add
functions to the last comparison window.
improved_commit_message: Refactored Function Comparison implementation to use a MatchedFunctionComparisonModel, enhancing comparison functionality and UI consistency.
change_summary: This commit introduces a new model for function comparisons that allows multiple target functions to be associated with a single source function, providing greater flexibility in function comparisons. Changes were made to the GUI components to adapt to this new model, and several deprecated methods were removed. The handling of adding and removing functions to/from comparisons was also improved.
hints: Replaced FunctionComparison model with a MatchedFunctionComparisonModel to better handle multiple matches.
Updated GUI components to reflect changes in how functions are compared.
Refactored service methods to accommodate new data structures.
Ensured consistency across user interactions by updating relevant event handlers.
Modified tests to validate the new behavior of function comparisons.

+package ghidra.app.context;
+
+import java.util.Set;
+
+import docking.ActionContext;
+import ghidra.program.model.listing.Function;
+
+/**
+ * A "mix-in" interface that specific implementers of {@link ActionContext} may also implement if
+ * they can supply functions in their action context. Actions that want to work on functions
+ * can look for this interface, which can used in a variety of contexts.
+ */
+public interface FunctionSupplierContext extends ActionContext {
+
+	/**
+	 * Returns true if this context can supply one or more functions. 
+	 * @return true if this context can supply one or more functions
+	 */
+	public boolean hasFunctions();
+
+	/**
+	 * Returns the set of functions that this context object can supply.
+	 * @return the set of functions that this context object can supply
+	 */
+	public Set<Function> getFunctions();
+}

change_summary: This commit cleans up the drag-and-drop handling code, removing redundant methods and comments that do not provide value. The logic is simplified by removing drag-related methods that were no-ops and consolidating feedback mechanisms.
hints: Removed empty methods such as dragCanceled and move in several classes.
Consolidated drag feedback methods to avoid redundancy.
Standardized the way drop handling responds to success or cancellation.

orig_commit_message: Refactor HighSymbol mutability
improved_commit_message: Refactor mutability handling in DecompileCallback and related classes
change_summary: The functionality for handling mutability of symbols and addresses has been consolidated and refactored. The previous methods for checking if a symbol is read-only or volatile have been replaced with a mutability system using constants. This improves the clarity and maintenance of the codebase, ensuring a centralized definition for mutability states.
hints: Replaced multiple isReadOnly and isVolatile methods with a single getMutability method returning an enum-like value.
Introduced MutabilitySettingsDefinition class for better mutability state management.
Removed redundant inline checks for read-only and volatile states in favor of a centralized approach using MemoryBlock checks.
Eliminated the outdated isReadOnlyNoData and isVolatileNoData methods, simplifying the logic in DecompileCallback.

orig_commit_message:
GP-4193 DWARFLine support, remove DWARF Line analyzer, misc fixes

Refactor the old DWARF line code used by the line analyzer.
Fix v4 location list reading when there was an empty range entry.
Defer applying the ELF program address fixup value until a DWARF address(held in a long) is converted into a Ghidra address.
Fix v5 location list reading - add missing DW_LLE_default_location impl.
improved_commit_message: Add DWARF source line information script
change_summary: Introduced a new script to extract and add source file line number information from DWARF debugging data to the current binary in Ghidra. This helps enhance the debugging experience by linking code execution back to the source lines.
hints: Created a new Ghidra script named DWARFLineInfoScript.
Used DWARFSectionProvider to fetch DWARF sections from the current program.
Implemented source line information extraction by reading from DWARF debug line entries.
Added comments containing the source file name and line number at corresponding locations in the binary.
